title: Two Kinds of Nothing: What Insignificant Results in Finance Actually Show
abstract: arXiv:2608.30490v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Claims of the form "we find no evidence that X affects Y" appear throughout the applied finance literature, yet whether such a claim contains evidence of absence or absence of evidence depends entirely on its confidence interval. The term "statistically insignificant" is routinely read to mean zero economic effect. However, a more honest description is that zero could not be rejected along with a range of other coefficient effect sizes. The crucial question is whether effect sizes in that range are consequential. This note distinguishes two kinds of insignificant results that are indistinguishable in a standard regression table: bounded null claims where the intervals reject effect sizes of consequence and thus represent a genuine finding, and vacuous null claims where even consequential effects remain unrejected and therefore establish nothing. translated_title: 两种“无”：金融学中不显著结果究竟表明了什么
translated_abstract: “我们发现没有证据表明X影响Y”这类论断在应用金融文献中随处可见，然而此类论断究竟包含“不存在的证据”还是“证据的缺失”，完全取决于其置信区间。“统计上不显著”这一术语通常被解读为经济效应为零，然而更诚实的描述是：零效应无法被拒绝，同时一系列其他系数效应大小同样无法被拒绝。关键问题在于该区间内的效应大小是否具有重要影响。本文区分了在标准回归表格中无法区分的两种不显著结果：有界零假设论断——其置信区间排除了具有重要影响的效应大小，因而代表了一个真正的发现；以及空洞零假设论断——即使具有重要影响的效应也未被拒绝，因此什么也没有确立。我提出了一套用于应用金融回归结果的最小报告标准。
tldr: 本文区分了金融实证研究中在回归表中无法区分的两种不显著结果——置信区间排除了重要效应的“有界零假设”（构成真正发现）与连重要效应都无法排除的“空洞零假设”（毫无发现），并据此提出了一套应用金融回归结果的最小报告标准。
en_tdlr: This paper distinguishes two kinds of statistically insignificant results in finance that look identical in regression tables—bounded null claims whose intervals reject consequential effect sizes (a genuine finding) versus vacuous null claims that leave even consequential effects unrejected (establishing nothing)—and proposes a minimal reporting standard for regression results in applied finance.
